title: the attach by the citation's collection and the person's name
line: the fallback that matches a page to a step by the person's name requires the page's own collection to be the citation's holder collection, whatever checklist row the citation sits under: two citations of one row at the same holder are not each other's record, a page of neither citation's collection matches nothing, and a birth page of the church-register collection reaches its principal's church-register steps and her birth-record search step alike, never her parents' steps

steps.say: one person's three death-record citations at the same holder: two Kentucky collections and an Ohio one

expect.why: a Kentucky death index page matches only the Kentucky death index citation's step, never the death records citation's nor the Ohio one at the same holder
a page of the death records collection, as the holders registry titles it, matches only the death records citation's step
an Ohio death index page matches only the Ohio citation's step
a page of a collection neither citation names matches nothing

steps.say: the grandmother's baseline decided on the owner's word, so her searches open, the birth record's among them

expect.why: her birth-record search step is planned

steps.say: her birth page of the church-register collection, saved from FamilySearch and attached from the inbox

expect.why: the page reaches four steps, all hers: three church-register citations of the collection it came from and the birth-record search

notes.has: the citation's own collection at its holder

expect.why: a church-register citation of the collection is logged found with the page, the reason naming the collection, though the page's own event is a birth and its row is not the birth row

notes.has: the row's kind and the person's name

expect.why: the search step, with no citation of its own, is reached by the row's kind as before
her father's church-register citation of the same collection is not reached: the page's principal is not him, and his own page in the entry is his record
